A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same catastrophe-avoidance research despite the changed title and substantial revision. The text, equations, figures, algorithms, and appendices are readable and support comparison: Appendices A–C in v2 and A–E in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports mathematical constructions, algorithms, and proofs, including its appendices. It contains no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V3 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. Its figures illustrate models and constructions rather than measured outcomes.

M1.justification: V2's Algorithm 1 initially collects mentor examples and then selects consistent local policies, querying when no previously queried state is nearby. V3 replaces this with randomized Hedge over policy covers, query-dependent weight updates, and a proximity check restricted to examples supporting the proposed action. It also introduces a one-versus-rest implementation for multiple actions and a query-capped variant. V2's bucket algorithm is retained as v3's Algorithm 4.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or empirical tasks. The new adversarial and smoothed-state regimes concern theoretical assumptions, not additional evaluated data or scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. Hedge becomes a method component in v3, while comparisons with standard online learning are theoretical.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to horizons, query rules, and state-generation assumptions belong to the algorithms and theoretical guarantees.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness tests, or case studies. V3's adaptive-adversary arguments and threshold example are theoretical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated runs, confidence intervals, or statistical estimates. Their probabilistic bounds and expectations are mathematical guarantees.

E6.justification: Neither version contains measured performance results or empirical findings. Changes to regret and query bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2's Natarajan/PAC/r-locality theorem is replaced by smoothed-VC and adversarial-Littlestone results, with new cover definitions, Hedge analysis, action-specific packing arguments, adaptive-adversary reasoning, and multiclass proofs. The retained 1D theorem receives a revised product-to-sum argument and bound under local generalization, whose formulation already appeared in v2's Remark B.1. The new proofs also contain algebraic inconsistencies: Lemma B.3 starts from an invalid equality, and the derivation of Theorem 5.2 drops a log(1/epsilon) factor.

C1.justification: V2 emphasizes learnability with bounded Natarajan dimension and additional locality, alongside a separate 1D result. V3 makes the central claim that catastrophe avoidance with mentor help and local generalization is no harder than standard online learning under the stated regimes. It also presents the retained threshold-capable algorithm as a separation between the two learning settings. The general impossibility claim remains.

C2.justification: V3 adds a substantive explanation of local generalization versus Lipschitz continuity, including how a suboptimal mentor can recommend poorly transferable actions (Figure 2). It reinterprets the 1D result through its separation from standard online learning. V2's limitations concerning r-locality and i.i.d. states are replaced by discussion of cover-construction cost, the unresolved finite-VC fully adversarial case, and the reliability of the distance-based generalization assumption.

D1.justification: V3 documents Hedge's query probability and learning-rate parameterization, including its conversion from the cited algorithm in Appendix B.1. Section 6 newly states an Omega(|tilde-Pi|T) computational cost plus cover construction. Neither version supplies executable code, implementation measurements, or data-access resources.

R1.justification: V2's contextual-bandit and compound-growth positioning gives way to substantial discussion of online learning, smoothed analysis, and active learning. V3 adds relevant work on Littlestone dimension, Hedge, adaptive smoothing, and label-efficient queries, including Haghtalab et al. and Russo et al., as well as AI-risk literature. Much of the irreversible-cost discussion is retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, model exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around online learning. V3 adds dedicated assumptions and standard-online-learning subsections, makes related work a standalone section, and adds a main-text proof sketch. V2's Section 5 and its appendix proof are consolidated into Appendix D, while the MDP open problem moves from the introduction to the conclusion.

P2.justification: V3 adds the table-form model comparison in Figure 1 and the three-panel assumption illustration in Figure 2; v2's hardness diagram remains as Figure 3. Algorithm displays are replaced, added, and relocated, including the bucket algorithm's move to Appendix D. Document-wide typography, margins, and title-page styling also change.

improvement.justification: V3 clarifies the connection to standard online learning and supplies an alternative to v2's restrictive r-locality construction. However, its smoothed-VC and adversarial-Littlestone guarantees do not uniformly subsume v2's arbitrary-i.i.d. setting. Moreover, the new Lemma B.3 induction contains an invalid equality, and Theorem 5.2's displayed derivation unjustifiably removes a logarithmic factor. These issues concern the documented support for central positive results, rather than proving those results false. The conceptual gains and unresolved proof problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
